summary: Regression of an enzyme's optimal pH from sequence, aggregated per protein from BRENDA measurements.
what_it_measures: The pH at which an enzyme shows maximal activity. Multiple BRENDA measurements per protein are aggregated to a median (pH ranges are averaged), then z-standardized (`phopt_median_standardized`).
assay_method: Literature-curated enzyme activity-vs-pH optima collected in BRENDA, the comprehensive enzyme-function database.
provenance: Parsed from the BRENDA JSON release (`ph_optimum` field), aggregated to a per-protein median with measurement counts recorded.
when_to_use: A protein-level regression testing whether embeddings encode the physicochemical environment an enzyme is adapted to; relevant to enzyme selection for a target pH.
caveats: pH optima are condition- and assay-dependent and sparsely measured; aggregating to a median discards spread. Values are standardized, so MAE is in standardized units.

citations.title: BRENDA, the ELIXIR core data resource in 2021: new developments and updates
